subtopic: Deciding whether to report a cheating friend
subtype: Approach: talking to the friend first [Action]
passage: I'm Naveena, and I'll tell you what I did when I saw my best friend Jeevika copy from a chit in the science test. I didn't go to the teacher. I waited till lunch, took her to the back steps, and said quietly, “I saw the chit, and it's been bothering me. I'm worried about you.” She went red and looked at her shoes. I asked why she'd done it, really, and I let her talk. She said she had panicked because she hadn't finished the syllabus. I told her I wasn't going to run to Ma'am, but I couldn't pretend I hadn't seen it, and she could tell Ma'am herself before the results came. Then I stayed sitting with her. Three days later she went to the staffroom. It wasn't easy, but she chose it. Jeevika's mother calls me the sensible girl of the class.

qa.q: Where did Naveena take Jeevika to talk?
qa.a: Naveena took her to the back steps at lunch.

qa.q: What was Jeevika feeling when she went red and looked at her shoes?
qa.a: Jeevika was embarrassed and ashamed, and she had panicked because she hadn't finished the syllabus.

qa.q: What could Naveena do if Jeevika does not confess?
qa.a: Naveena could tell a trusted adult or the teacher calmly, since she gave Jeevika a fair chance and fairness to other students still matters.

qa.q: How might the teacher see Jeevika coming to the staffroom?
qa.a: The teacher may appreciate the honesty and treat it more gently than a case of being caught, since Jeevika chose to come forward.

grounding: A teen privately tells her friend that copying worries her, asks why it happened and gives her a chance to fix it herself by confessing.

subtopic: Deciding whether to report a cheating friend
subtype: Approach: talking to the friend first [Action]
passage:
I'm Kishore, and I was in the library corner when Sharmila found Gayatri on Thursday. I wasn't trying to listen, but it was quiet.
Sharmila kept her voice low. “I saw you copy from the phone in the history test. I'm not going to go running to anyone. But it's been bothering me all day.” Gayatri went red and started to say she hadn't, then stopped.
Sharmila asked, “What happened? You're good at history.” Gayatri said she'd been up till two helping at her uncle's shop and hadn't studied a word.
Then Sharmila said, “Would you tell Mrs Nair yourself? I'll come with you if you want. I think it's better coming from you than from anyone else.”
Gayatri didn't answer right away. On Friday morning I saw them both outside the staffroom. I don't know what was said inside, but Gayatri came out looking lighter.

qa.a: She'd been up till two helping at her uncle's shop.

qa.q: What was Sharmila feeling before speaking to Gayatri?
qa.a: Sharmila felt uneasy and bothered all day, worried about both the cheating and her friend.

qa.q: What else could Sharmila have done if Gayatri refused?
qa.a: Give her a day to think, and if nothing changed, speak to Mrs Nair calmly as the next step.

qa.q: How might Gayatri have seen Sharmila's offer to go with her?
qa.a: Gayatri probably felt embarrassed but supported, since she got a chance to put it right herself with a friend beside her.

grounding: A classmate overhears a teen privately tell her friend the copying worries her, ask why, and offer her the chance to own up to the teacher herself.

subtopic: Deciding whether to report a cheating friend

passage:
Tuesday: In the science practical exam, Indu sees her friend Yashika copying readings from the student at the next table. Yashika doesn't notice her watching.
Tuesday evening: Indu thinks about telling the teacher. Then she thinks: Yashika deserves a chance to explain first, and to fix it herself.
Wednesday, after school: On the walk home, Indu says, “Yashika, I saw you copy the readings yesterday. It's worrying me. What happened?” Yashika is silent for a long time, then says her experiment failed twice and she panicked. Indu says, “Could you tell Ma'am and ask to redo it? I'll wait outside the lab.”
Thursday: Yashika tells the teacher. The teacher lets her redo the practical on Saturday, with a small deduction. Yashika sends Indu a message: “Thanks for not just reporting me."

qa.q: What did Yashika say had happened?
qa.a: Her experiment failed twice and she panicked.

qa.q: Why did Indu choose to speak to Yashika first?
qa.a: Indu felt Yashika deserved a chance to explain, and was worried and caring rather than wanting to get her in trouble.

qa.q: What could Indu do if Yashika had refused to tell the teacher?
qa.a: Explain that she would have to inform Ma'am herself, then do so calmly, since practical marks affect others too.

qa.q: How might Yashika feel about the way Indu handled it?
qa.a: Yashika feels grateful and relieved that she could own up herself instead of simply being reported.

grounding: Shows a teen privately telling her friend the copying worries her, asking why, and giving her the chance to confess to the teacher herself.
